title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 30-32 of 'Algèbre des figures'). A 'figure' F is a family of closed subsets of a space with these properties. Every point x of the support |F| lies in a smallest element A of F. The element A then has an 'open stratum' A° = A(F)°, namely A minus the union of the smaller elements of F. The intersection of two elements is a union of strata. Writing F' ≤ F means F' refines F: same support, every A' ∈ F' lies in a smallest element of F, and every element of F is a union of strata of F'. A subfigure G ≤ F is a downward-closed piece, closed in the order. G' is a subdivision of G with |G'| = |G|, and is compatible with F (G' ≪ F). The construction under study is F' = G' ∪ (F \ G): subdivide G and leave the rest of F untouched.

Page 30 proved that F' is a figure and began proving that F' refines F. This page finishes that proof. If A ∈ F' \ G' = F \ G and B ∈ F, then A ∩ B is a union of strata of F. It remains to see that each stratum (open stratum A°) of F is a union of strata of F'. Let A ∈ F. If A ∉ G, then A ∈ F \ G ⊂ F', and its stratum is a stratum of F'. If A ∈ G, then, since G' refines G, A° is a union of strata of G', which are strata of F'.

Corollary. The subdivisions F' of F of this form are characterized by the following equivalent properties.
- (a), crossed out and replaced by a marginal variant: F' is the largest (coarsest) subdivision of F inducing G' on G, for a suitable order ≤*.
- (b): the canonical map φ: F' → F, sending A' to the smallest element of F containing it, induces a bijection F' \ G' → F \ G.
- (c): for every A ∈ F \ G, the open stratum A° is an open stratum of F'.
- (d): F' ⊃ F \ G.

The marginal note says (b), (c), (d) are equivalent but (a) needs care. The planned cycle of proof is d ⇒ b ⇒ c ⇒ a ⇒ d.

The proof of d ⇒ b starts here. If F \ G ⊂ F', then φ restricted to F \ G is the identity. So one must show F \ G = F' \ G'; this is completed on p. 32 using |G| = |G'| and the downward-closedness of G and G'.

Purpose: a combinatorial lemma on extending a subdivision of a closed sub-stratification to the whole stratified space in the minimal way. This is the analogue, for poset-indexed stratifications by closed sets, of extending a subdivision of a subcomplex without touching the other cells. It serves the formal 'algebra of figures' (stratified spaces / tame topology) of the 1986 notes.
errors: Statement (b) as transcribed reads 'F \ G' → F \ G'; it must be F' \ G' → F \ G. This is confirmed by the continuation on p. 32.
In the case split 'Si A ∉ G', alors A ∈ F'... Si A ∈ G' (comme G' ≤ G)', the intended conditions are A ∉ G and A ∈ G, since A is an element of F.

Gap: for A ∈ F \ G, the open stratum of A in F must be shown equal to its open stratum in F'. Its smaller elements change, since elements of G are replaced by those of G'. This is used tacitly here and deferred to a 'lemme plus bas' on p. 32.
Characterization (a) is struck through, and the marginal remark suggests Grothendieck doubted its equivalence or its formulation. The cycle d⇒b⇒c⇒a⇒d therefore rests on an unsettled (a).

ideas.what: Gluing a subdivision G' of a subfigure G with the untouched remainder F \ G to get a refinement F' of F
ideas.modern_name: Extension of a refinement of a closed sub-stratification (relative subdivision of a poset-stratified space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in PL topology and stratification theory (subdivision of subcomplexes extended to complexes)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of 'tame topology' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but no such lemma is published

ideas.what: Characterization of such 'minimal' subdivisions: φ bijective off G; outside strata stay open strata; F' contains F \ G; maximality among subdivisions inducing G'
ideas.modern_name: Minimal/coarsest refinement extending a given refinement on a closed union of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not specifically credited; standard-type combinatorics of stratifications

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine combinatorial lemma on refinements of closed-set stratifications. It is part of an unpublished formal framework, but the content itself would not surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: (b) should read F' \ G' → F \ G (bijection), not F \ G' → F \ G.
'Si A ∉ G'' / 'Si A ∈ G'' in the case split likely refer to G (A ∈ F), and the parenthesis reads '(comme G' ≤ G)'.
'[-Rédi-]mats' is likely the struck 'Réciproquement' / 'Rest(e) à...'; the sense is 'il reste à voir que une strate de F est réunion de strates de F''.
Marginal note near the Corollaire: '* on pose ... au plus ... des subdivisions de F induisant G' sur G' defines the order ≤* used in the reformulated (a).
Margin note: 'les conditions b), c), d) sont équivalentes, mais a) ...' (a) is flagged as problematic.
